newsitem.title: UK: GEC boosted by finance chief appointment.
newsitem.headline: GEC boosted by finance chief appointment.

text.p: General Electric Co Plc shares were the top performers in the FTSE 100 index by late morning on Tuesday as the market welcomed the appointment of John Mayo as new finance director, analysts and dealers said.
GEC shares were up 13p or 3.6 percent to 357p by 1025 GMT in active trade of more than five million shares.

Amid talk of further restructuring at GEC, Zeneca Group Plc's Mayo was regarded as a leading finance director who would bring to GEC his experience of the de-merger of the drug group from Imperial Chemical Industries Plc.
"With his involvement in the break-up of ICI, people are just putting two and two together," said one dealer.
Yet not all analysts were immediately convinced the appointment would be positive for the stock in the near term.

"It is politically a very good appointment in terms of his reputation...but the key issue is how GEC restructures itself and how quickly it improves the return to shareholders," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
"I don't think it makes much difference to that issue"
Earlier GEC managing director George Simpson said he was pleased to welcome Mayo to the company.

"John has a well deserved reputation as one of this country's best finance directors," Simpson said. "His experience with Warburg and ICI...are highly relevant to the challenges and opportunities now facing GEC. I look forward to working with him."
